text: Table stores: one row per physical shop of the chain. city is the German city name with umlauts (München, Köln, Nürnberg).
stores.opened_on: the date the shop opened.
Table customers: one row per customer account. city is where the customer lives, spelled like stores.city (München, not Munich).
customers.signup_date: the date the account was created.
customers.deleted_at: set when the customer deleted the account (soft delete). An active customer has deleted_at IS NULL. Their old orders stay in orders.
Table products: the catalogue. name is unique per category, not across categories.
products.list_price_cents: today's list price in euro cents. It is NOT the price customers paid; for that use order_items.unit_price_cents.
products.is_active: false when the product is no longer offered. Inactive products can still appear in past orders.
Table orders: one row per order, online or in a store. ordered_at is a UTC timestamp.
orders.channel: 'online' or 'store'. Online orders have store_id NULL.
orders.status: 'paid', 'cancelled' (never charged) or 'refunded' (fully refunded). Only 'paid' orders count as sales.
Table order_items: the lines of an order. qty units at unit_price_cents each (the price actually paid, in euro cents), minus discount_cents for the whole line.
Table returns: items sent back from paid orders. refund_cents is the money given back for that return, in euro cents. returned_at is a UTC timestamp.
Business rule, revenue: sum over order_items of qty * unit_price_cents - discount_cents, for orders with status = 'paid' only, divided by 100 to get euros. Cancelled and refunded orders never count.
Business rule, net revenue: revenue minus refund_cents from returns (divided by 100 for euros). Assign a return to the period of its returned_at.
Business rule: every *_cents column is euro cents. Report money in euros, rounded to 2 decimals, unless cents are asked for.
Business rule, units sold: sum of order_items.qty on paid orders.
Business rule, average order value (AOV): revenue divided by the number of distinct paid orders, in euros.
Business rule, dates: a year or month refers to orders.ordered_at (or returns.returned_at for returns). Quarters are calendar quarters: Q3 is July to September.

Business rule: a question about the customer base (where customers live, when they signed up, how many there are) means active customers, deleted_at IS NULL. A question about orders or sales includes every customer who ordered, deleted or not.
